solutionReasonableness.problemFit: Correcting the catalog delete and temporary-promotion response shapes before a literal fixture DAG is built targets the demonstrated false-green source without changing product behavior.
solutionReasonableness.simplerAlternativeAssessment: The six-path owner/edge/consumer correction plus one governed HTTP handoff test is smaller and safer than admitting the catalog/checker/materializer/workload conversion now; no new API, capability or dispatcher is justified.
solutionReasonableness.costFit: Repairing one stale manifest anchor is a localized admission correction. Bypassing it or compensating with runtime evidence would create disproportionate scope and violate the serialized design boundary.

conclusion.summary: Round 2 independently confirms the M-000/M-001/S-001 design repairs and preserved no-runtime boundary, but finds one new blocking manifest-to-design anchor mismatch. The current manifest cannot pass its own granularity admission.
